title.narrative: Danish Peace and Stabilisation Programme West Africa 2025-2028

description.narrative: The overall objective of the support is: instability in key border areas in West Africa is mitigated through local and regional capacity development. The focus is on border areas at risk of expansion of violent extremist organisations (VEO). The PSP WA covers seven countries, including Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger in Central Sahel, and Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana and Togo in Coastal West Africa (CWA). Hence, the programmatic focus on the Sahel in the PSP WA predecessor programmes is expanded to also include these coastal West African countries. The border areas between Burkina Faso and the coastal countries Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana and Togo, is of particular interest in this phase of the programme, as this is the area where the spill-over of instability from the Sahel towards the coastal countries of West Africa is currently most pronounced. Nigeria is not included as a target country at this stage. However, the country has a regional significance, due to the security situation in the North West of the country and cross-border dynamics with Benin and Niger, its relation to transnational crime networks, and its role as the headquarters of the regional organisation in West Africa ECOWAS. In addition, Nigeria is particularly relevant due to its economic and military power in the region.
